title: Regular Expressions
summary: Finding and taking apart text with java.util.regex - Pattern and Matcher, matches versus find, groups and named groups, looping over every match, replacing with a function, splitting, flags such as CASE_INSENSITIVE, the escaping rules in Java strings, and when a regular expression is the wrong tool.

cards.q: What is the difference between `matches()` and `find()`?
cards.a:
`matches()` must match the whole text; `find()` looks for the next place the pattern occurs anywhere

Use `matches()` to validate a whole string and `find()` to search inside one. `lookingAt()` is the one that matches only at the start.

`.` means "any character", so every character is a separator

The argument of `split` is a regex; escape the dot as `"\\."` to split on a literal dot. Trailing empty parts are dropped, which leaves nothing.

cards.q: How is the regex `\d+` written in a Java string literal?
cards.a:
`"\\d+"`

Java strings use backslash for their own escapes, so each regex backslash is doubled.
